rows.n: mi
rows.b: Short for mile or miles.

rows.n: miasma
miaul
mini-batch
rows.b: A small batch used in practice, since whole-dataset batches would never fit in memory.

rows.n: mixed precision training
rows.b: Training with a blend of 16-bit and 32-bit numbers to go faster and use less memory without hurting quality.

rows.n: mixture of experts
rows.b: A design with many small specialist networks where only a few activate per token, growing capacity without growing cost per token.

rows.n: MMLU
rows.b: A famous 57-subject multiple-choice test of general knowledge, from math to law to history.

rows.n: mobile deployment
rows.b: Shrinking and tuning a model so it runs well on phones with limited memory and battery.

rows.n: model hub
rows.b: Any repository where trained models are published for others to download and use.

rows.n: model license
rows.b: The legal terms saying what you may do with a model — commercial use, modification, and redistribution rules.

rows.n: model merging
rows.b: Blending the weights of two trained models to combine their skills without retraining.

rows.n: model parallel
rows.b: Splitting the model itself across GPUs when it is too big for one card.

rows.n: model quantization
rows.b: The deployment-time step of converting weights to fewer bits for speed and size.

rows.n: model server
rows.b: Software built to load models and serve many users efficiently, with batching and caching.

rows.n: model versioning
rows.b: Labeling each trained model, like v1 and v2, so you can track and roll between them.

rows.n: momentum
rows.b: An optimizer trick that keeps updates moving in a consistent direction, smoothing out noisy gradients.

rows.n: monitoring
rows.b: Watching a deployed model for errors, slowness, and quality drift.

rows.n: multi-head attention
rows.b: Running several attention operations in parallel so the model can track different kinds of word relationships at once.

rows.n: multi-query attention
rows.b: The extreme version: every query head shares a single key-value head for maximum generation speed.

rows.n: multiple choice eval
rows.b: Testing by asking the model to pick from options, scored by which choice gets the highest probability.
